**Takeaway:** NVDA's gross margin fell sharply in Q1 fiscal 2026 (quarter ending April 2025), dropping to [[F22]] from [[F21]] in the prior quarter. The data does not show why.

**Trend across all periods shown.** Gross margin had been declining gradually from [[F18]] in Q1 fiscal 2025 through [[F21]] in Q4 fiscal 2025. In Q1 fiscal 2026 it dropped to [[F22]], the lowest point in the eight-quarter window. It then recovered to [[F23]] in Q2 fiscal 2026 and continued improving through [[F24]] and [[F25]] in Q3 and Q4 fiscal 2026, though it had not yet returned to the Q1 fiscal 2025 level by the end of the window.

**What is strong and what is weak.** The Q1 fiscal 2026 quarter is the clear outlier: gross margin, operating margin ([[F30]]), and net margin ([[F38]]) all hit their lows in that quarter simultaneously, while revenue continued to grow sequentially ([[F14]] vs. [[F13]]). The recovery in subsequent quarters is notable—by Q4 fiscal 2026, gross margin ([[F25]]) had nearly matched the Q3 fiscal 2025 level ([[F20]]), and operating margin ([[F33]]) had returned to the Q1 fiscal 2025 level ([[F26]]).

**Counterpoint.** Revenue growth remained robust in Q1 fiscal 2026 at [[F8]] quarter-over-quarter and [[F9]] year-over-year, so the margin compression occurred alongside accelerating top-line expansion rather than a demand shortfall. This suggests the margin dip may have been a cost-side or mix event rather than a structural deterioration in pricing power.

**What the data cannot tell.** The data does not show why gross margin fell in Q1 fiscal 2026. No management attribution or claim is available in the evidence provided. The figures shown do not include a cost-of-revenue breakdown, segment-level margins, or any commentary that would explain the driver.

> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** A one-time charge or product-mix shift compressed margins in that single quarter, given the sharp V-shaped recovery to [[F23]] the very next quarter while revenue kept growing.

> **Unverified hypothesis (low confidence):** A change in revenue recognition or inventory accounting affected the quarter, given that operating margin and net margin also dropped to their window lows ([[F30]], [[F38]]) in the same period.
